label_status: owner-approved 2026-10-15; labelled from the pack, before any run of this ticker
rationale: Undisputed quality (operating margin about 29%, ten steady years) at a premium price (P/E about 29, EV/EBIT about 30) for low single-digit growth: 'great company, priced for perfection'. STRONG_CASE would need the price to support interest too.
must_find: The valuation is high relative to the company's growth (a premium multiple, for example a P/E around 29).
must_not: Treats Coca-Cola's changed FY2017-FY2018 figures (recasts filed 2019-2021) as evidence of accounting manipulation.

label_status: owner-approved 2026-10-15; labelled from the pack, before any run of this ticker; the most debatable label
rationale: Strong growth, but GAAP operating losses every year (about -1.24 billion TTM), stock-based compensation about 30% of revenue that carries the positive free cash flow, and a price of about 22 times revenue that requires exceptional execution.
must_find: Snowflake is loss-making on a GAAP basis (operating or net losses).
Stock-based compensation is a large share of revenue, or the positive free cash flow rests largely on non-cash stock-based compensation.
must_not: States as a fact that Snowflake had no debt (zero debt) before FY2024.

label_status: owner-approved 2026-10-15; labelled after one real run of this ticker (verdict WEAK_CASE), so possibly anchored on it
rationale: Shrinking revenue, repeated multi-billion impairments (Q2 FY2025, Q2 FY2026), a TTM operating loss and the 2017-2019 restatement history; cheap on free cash flow (about 7x) if the charges are non-cash. Not RED_FLAGGED: the accounting failures are seven years old and filings have been timely since.
must_find: Earlier reported FY2016-FY2017 figures (for example operating cash flow or operating income) were restated.
The 8-K Item 4.02 non-reliance notices or the late annual report (the NT 10-K, the 10-K filed about 160 days after year end).
must_not: Describes the large Q2 operating losses as cash losses, although operating cash flow in those quarters was positive.

label_status: drafted by Claude Code from the pack under the owner's delegation; reviewed in two independent reviews (2026-10-16); not blind-labelled by the owner
rationale: Flat revenue (3-year CAGR about 0.6%) but operating margins of 12-21% over ten years (17-19% in the last three) and about 20 billion of free cash flow over the last twelve months, at a price of about 6.7 times earnings and 3.7 times free cash flow (yield about 27%), with about 84 billion of debt. The price assumes decline; the case holds if cash flows stay near today's level. Calling it a weak case would mean the evidence does not support interest even at this price.
must_find: Revenue is roughly flat or growing very slowly (low single-digit or near-zero growth).
The valuation is low: for example a P/E around 7, or a free cash flow yield around 20% or more.
must_not: Describes the stock as expensive or says the price requires strong growth.

label_status: drafted by Claude Code from the pack under the owner's delegation; reviewed in two independent reviews (2026-10-16); not blind-labelled by the owner. Strict on purpose: only red-flagged counts, so a constant 'weak case' cannot pass it
rationale: Liquidity and dilution carry the label: cash of about 0.16 billion against an operating cash outflow of about 0.48 billion over the last twelve months (roughly four months of burn), an operating loss larger than revenue every year since FY2023 (TTM about -1.29 billion on 0.74 billion of revenue), and a share count up about fourfold since FY2020 (0.35 billion diluted then, 1.40 billion on the latest cover page). History, not a current red flag on its own: the 2021 non-reliance notice with late annual and quarterly reports, the 2022 amendment of the FY2020 annual report that extended the material weakness in internal control to 2018 and 2019, and a change of auditor in 2022; annual reports have been on time since. Checked on EDGAR on 2026-10-16: the amended annual reports of 2017-05-01, 2023-05-01 and 2025-04-30 only add the Part III information (executive pay and governance, no new numbers) and are not red flags.
must_find: Liquidity is the threat: the cash on hand (about 0.16 billion) is small against the cash the business burns (operating cash outflow about 0.48 billion a year) or against losses larger than revenue.
The share count has risen steeply (about fourfold since 2020), diluting shareholders.
must_not: Describes Plug Power as profitable or its free cash flow as positive.
Treats the amended annual reports that only add Part III information (executive pay and governance) as accounting red flags.
